section_entries.label: Background and coefficient design
section_entries.mathematical_role: Defines normalized gap extremals, states the conditional theorem and threshold criterion, surveys coefficient improvements, introduces the paper's simplified prime-divisor perturbation, and records method limits.

unit_result_entry.title: From divisor weights to Feng–Wu's prime-moment enrichment
unit_result_entry.why_material: Shows how successive coefficient designs enrich a basic divisor weight with shape polynomials and prime-factor moments, and identifies an equivalent one-prime power-sum representation whose calculations are simpler.

unit_dependency_entry.context_note: Overlaps the historical tail of u01 so the progression from the Conrey–Ghosh–Gonek family through Bui–Milinovich–Ng to Feng–Wu remains coherent.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Normalized zero gaps and the Montgomery–Odlyzko threshold criterion
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: Connects pair-correlation motivation, the conditional target bounds, and the functional h(c) whose crossing of 1 turns a coefficient choice into a large- or small-gap conclusion; it also records early coefficient choices and attained bounds.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Simplified coefficient perturbation and intrinsic threshold limits
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: Introduces the paper's base polynomial plus prime-divisor correction, explains the tradeoff between generality and explicit evaluability, and distinguishes coefficient optimization from known limits of the Montgomery–Odlyzko framework.

related_synthesis_entries.claim: Adding a prime-divisor polynomial correction expands the quadratic and shifted products into systematically classifiable zero-, one-, and two-correction interactions, each reduced by the same sum-to-integral toolkit.
related_synthesis_entries.limit: The extracted formulas support the interaction pattern more securely than exact constants, integration bounds, or exponents, which require scan verification.
